about: What a user can do, and how each client reaches it. Every API route is a capability here or listed in internalRoutes; each surface names its calls (SDK methods, CLI commands, MCP tools), or says in a sentence why it has none, and mcpHosted says when the hosted MCP server lacks a tool the local one has. A capability counts as covered when its calls reach its routes; split one when a client reaches only some of them. Nobody should need the dashboard: a capability every client lacks is a gap to close, and sessionOnly says why a person still has to be in the loop. Checked by packages/sdk/src/__tests__/capabilities.test.ts, packages/mcp/src/__tests__/capabilities.test.ts and apps/cli-rs (cli::capabilities).

internalRoutes./api/edge/*: the tunnel edge's own calls, with its secret
internalRoutes./api/report: the report form on preview pages
internalRoutes./api/site-switch: carries a browser session between webhooks.cc and mailhooks.cc
internalRoutes./api/go/*: guest endpoints on the landing page
internalRoutes./api/auth/*: the device login behind `whk auth login`
internalRoutes./api/oauth2/*: the OAuth server behind the remote MCP server and `whk auth login`
internalRoutes./api/attachments/*: signed attachment links inside deliveries: the link is the permission
internalRoutes./api/account/mfa/*: two-factor sign-in, which belongs to the browser
